opening.text: When you buy a new car, there is a manual in the glove box. It tells you what fuel to use and what to avoid. Ignore it, and the engine suffers. The maker knows the machine. God made our bodies, and He gave us a manual. It is called the Word of Wisdom. It tells us what helps the body and what harms it.

mainMessage.text: The Word of Wisdom is God's care for our bodies and spirits. It comes with real promises.

blocks.text: **A plan for healthy living** God gave this counsel in 1833. He gave it out of love, as a principle with a promise.

To be sent greeting; not by commandment or constraint, but by revelation and the word of wisdom, showing forth the order and will of God in the temporal salvation of all saints in the last days— Given for a principle with promise, adapted to the capacity of the weak and the weakest of all saints, who are or can be called saints.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Principles and Promises” from the October 2016 general conference.
In 1833 the Lord revealed to the Prophet Joseph Smith a plan for healthy living.
It is a plan for healthy living.
**The promises are real** The Lord tied great blessings to this counsel. They are for body and mind and spirit.

And all saints who remember to keep and do these sayings, walking in obedience to the commandments, shall receive health in their navel and marrow to their bones; And shall find wisdom and great treasures of knowledge, even hidden treasures;
President Boyd K. Packer, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Word of Wisdom: The Principle and the Promises” from the April 1996 general conference.
Honor the principle of the Word of Wisdom and you will receive the promised blessings.
Honor it, and the blessings follow.
**A law for the spirit too** The Word of Wisdom is about more than food and drink. Paul said our body is the temple of the Holy Ghost.

What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
The Word of Wisdom is a spiritual law.
It blesses the spirit.
**Freedom, not chains** Some habits start as a choice and end as a chain. The Lord's counsel keeps us free.
Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
Addiction to any substance enslaves not only the physical body but the spirit as well.
It keeps us free.
**Good things, used well** God gave us herbs and fruits to use with prudence and thanksgiving. Good sense matters in health and in medicine.

And again, verily I say unto you, all wholesome herbs God hath ordained for the constitution, nature, and use of man— Every herb in the season thereof, and every fruit in the season thereof; all these to be used with prudence and thanksgiving.
President Boyd K. Packer, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Word of Wisdom: The Principle and the Promises” from the April 1996 general conference.
Young people, learn to use moderation and common sense in matters of health and nutrition, and particularly in medication.
Use good things wisely.
**Choose to be different** Living the Word of Wisdom can set us apart. The Lord promised strength and protection to those who do.

And shall run and not be weary, and shall walk and not faint. And I, the Lord, give unto them a promise, that the destroying angel shall pass by them, as the children of Israel, and not slay them. Amen.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
Choose to be different; you will be blessed both physically and spiritually.
Be different, and be blessed.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to follow the Word of Wisdom and were blessed. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Daniel's choice

blocks.text: Daniel was taken to serve in a foreign king's court. He was offered the king's rich food and wine.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself. And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king’s meat.
Daniel decided in his heart before the test came. That is why he stood firm. His choice was quiet, and the results showed.

application.text: First, decide now, before the test comes, what you will do. Second, write down one habit that helps your body, like rest, water or good food. Third, begin it this week.

opening.text: On a steep mountain road, there is a guardrail at the edge. It doesn't stop the drive. It makes the drive safe. Nobody complains about the guardrail when they look down at the drop. The Word of Wisdom is a guardrail. It keeps us on the road and lets us go farther with confidence.

mainMessage.text: The Word of Wisdom is a guardrail given by a loving God. It protects us so we can travel with confidence.

blocks.text: **Built by someone who cares** Guardrails are built by people who know the road. The Lord gave this counsel for our good.

To be sent greeting; not by commandment or constraint, but by revelation and the word of wisdom, showing forth the order and will of God in the temporal salvation of all saints in the last days— Given for a principle with promise, adapted to the capacity of the weak and the weakest of all saints, who are or can be called saints.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Principles and Promises” from the October 2016 general conference.
In 1833 the Lord revealed to the Prophet Joseph Smith a plan for healthy living.
It was built with care.
**The view at the top** The guardrail lets us reach the best views. The Lord promised wisdom and health to those who keep His counsel.

And all saints who remember to keep and do these sayings, walking in obedience to the commandments, shall receive health in their navel and marrow to their bones; And shall find wisdom and great treasures of knowledge, even hidden treasures;
President Boyd K. Packer, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Word of Wisdom: The Principle and the Promises” from the April 1996 general conference.
Honor the principle of the Word of Wisdom and you will receive the promised blessings.
The view is worth it.
**Protecting more than the body** The rail guards the whole traveler, body and spirit. Our body is a temple of the Holy Ghost.

What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
The Word of Wisdom is a spiritual law.
It guards body and spirit.
**Free to go on** A car that goes over the edge isn't free. It's lost. The guardrail keeps us free to keep driving.
Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
Addiction to any substance enslaves not only the physical body but the spirit as well.
It keeps us free to go on.
**A road meant to be used** The road isn't only for avoiding things. God gave us good food to enjoy with thanks and good judgment.

And again, verily I say unto you, all wholesome herbs God hath ordained for the constitution, nature, and use of man— Every herb in the season thereof, and every fruit in the season thereof; all these to be used with prudence and thanksgiving.
President Boyd K. Packer, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Word of Wisdom: The Principle and the Promises” from the April 1996 general conference.
Young people, learn to use moderation and common sense in matters of health and nutrition, and particularly in medication.
Use the road well.
**Drive on and don't tire** The Lord promised those who keep His counsel that they would run and not be weary. He also promised protection.

And shall run and not be weary, and shall walk and not faint. And I, the Lord, give unto them a promise, that the destroying angel shall pass by them, as the children of Israel, and not slay them. Amen.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Addiction or Freedom” from the October 1988 general conference.
Choose to be different; you will be blessed both physically and spiritually.
No weariness on this road.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their family held to a standard that others did not. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Rechabites refuse wine

blocks.text: The prophet Jeremiah set wine before the family of the Rechabites and invited them to drink. They said no.

And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine. But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever:
They were steady even when it was offered to them right then. Many generations kept the same promise. A firm family standard can last.

application.text: First, think about where your guardrails are. Second, talk with your family about one standard you all hold. Third, say it out loud, so everyone is clear.

story.title: John the Baptist

blocks.text: Before John was born, an angel told his father what kind of life he would live.
For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.
John's life was set apart from the start. He was filled with the Holy Ghost. A clean life made room for the Spirit.

story.title: The stripling warriors

blocks.text: A group of young men went to battle. They had been taught by their mothers. They were known for how they lived.

And they were all young men, and they were exceedingly valiant for courage, and also for strength and activity; but behold, this was not all—they were men who were true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted. Yea, they were men of truth and soberness, for they had been taught to keep the commandments of God and to walk uprightly before him.
Their strength came from how they were taught and how they lived. They kept the commandments, and they were true.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when God strengthened them as they kept His commandments. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi's family in the wilderness

blocks.text: Nephi's family traveled through a hard wilderness with little food. Yet they were strong.

And so great were the blessings of the Lord upon us, that while we did live upon raw meat in the wilderness, our women did give plenty of suck for their children, and were strong, yea, even like unto the men; and they began to bear their journeyings without murmurings. And thus we see that the commandments of God must be fulfilled. And if it so be that the children of men keep the commandments of God he doth nourish them, and strengthen them, and provide means whereby they can accomplish the thing which he has commanded them; wherefore, he did provide means for us while we did sojourn in the wilderness.
The Lord nourished and strengthened them. He does the same for us when we do what He asks.

application.text: First, look at your habits like a homeowner. What needs repair? Second, fix one thing this week. Third, ask God for strength to keep at it.
